# cli { #wdm.cli }

`cli`

Command-line interface.

Every command reads ``data/raw/observations.csv`` and ``data/raw/subject.toml``
of this repository unless given other paths, so they run from any directory.

The everyday loop:

``daily``
    The morning routine: record the weigh-in (and waist, when due), fill in a
    day of food left unlogged, then validate, plan and log the plan.
``log`` (alias ``eat``)
    Add a meal, exercise energy or the step count to a day, and show what is
    left of today's prescription.
``plan``
    Run the controller and print a prescription for today.

Diagnostics:

``validate``
    Check a CSV before trusting anything built on it.
``fit-noise``
    Phase 1. Estimate observation and trend noise from your weight history.
``filter``
    Phase 2. Joint state and parameter estimation; writes state trajectories
    and figures.
``backtest``
    Score the filter's out-of-sample forecasts of every weigh-in.

Exercise energy:

``session-kcal``
    Estimate a named session's energy cost from a routine CSV (one row per
    exercise, no dates) -- for "I did Lower A today" rather than a full
    dated log entry.
``exercise-kcal``
    Estimate a lifting session's energy cost from a set-by-set log in a
    dated workout-tracker spreadsheet.

``demo``
    Run the whole pipeline on synthetic data with known ground truth. Useful for
    seeing what the output looks like before you have four months of your own,
    and for confirming the install works.

### cmd_daily { #wdm.cli.cmd_daily }

```python
cli.cmd_daily(args)
```

The morning routine: collect what is missing, then validate, plan and log.

In a terminal it asks, in order, for yesterday's food if that row has none,
this morning's weight, and the waist when one is due; a blank answer skips
the item. Values given as flags are not asked for, and ``--no-input`` turns
the questions off (for scripts), leaving only warnings.

### cmd_demo { #wdm.cli.cmd_demo }

```python
cli.cmd_demo(args)
```

End-to-end run on synthetic data with known ground truth.
